title: Complete monotonicity conjecture for even powers of Baskakov functions
statement:
Let $r>1$ be an even integer and let $\alpha>0$. Define

$$
f_{\alpha}^{[r]}(x)=(1+x)^{-r\alpha}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\binom{-\alpha}{k}^{r}\left(\frac{x}{1+x}\right)^{rk},\qquad x\geq 0.
$$

For positive $c$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, also define

$$
p_{n,k}^{[c]}(x)=\binom{-n/c}{k}\left(-cx\right)^k\left(1+cx\right)^{-n/c-k}
$$

and

$$
\psi_{n,c}^{[r]}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(p_{n,k}^{[c]}(x)\right)^r,\qquad x\geq 0.
$$

**Even-power complete-monotonicity conjecture.** The function $f_{\alpha}^{[r]}$ is completely monotonic on $[0,\infty)$. In particular, $\psi_{n,c}^{[r]}$ is completely monotonic on $[0,\infty)$. The paper presents this as a conjecture after noting that numerical simulations suggest the property for even $r$, while its results establish the case $r=2$; the general even-power case remains open in the supplied text.
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1104.2401](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.2401).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.7945

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).
source_name: Ulrich Abel, Wolfgang Gawronski and Thorsten Neuschel, “Complete Monotonicity and Zeros of Sums of Squared Baskakov Functions”, arXiv:1411.7945 (2014).
